content:
incident-bot: [ALERT] GPU pool eu-west-2 (pool-gpu-prod) 90% queued, autoscaler failing to provision. queued_requests=18k, avg_latency=12s, error_rate=2.8% :rotating_light:
liam-sre: oncall taking this. paging the autoscale rotation channel.
jenna-runtime: seeing a ton of KV-cache misses, TTL spike. Preserving current pods while we investigate — don’t drain.
matt-infra: grabbing cloud provider console now. API shows repeated 429s from provider for instance-creation calls. suspect provider rate limiting + leader election stall.
sara-oncall: customers hitting timeouts? carol, any external CS reports?
carol-cs: yes — two enterprise customers reported elevated 5xxs and long tails around 11:10–11:25. They’re in eu-west region. I’ve opened tickets and told them we’re on it.
liam-sre: quick assessment: autoscaler controller pod restarted itself 3x in last 20m (OOM?), leader lease not renewed -> controllers stopped issuing scale-up jobs. Meanwhile queue continued to grow, hitting router-level throttles.
opsbot: Deploy log: autoscaler:v2.4.1 deployed 2026-02-11T10:58Z by ci-bot. CrashLoop count=3.
jenna-runtime: stack traces attached to pod logs point to a GC spike in the runtime when evaluating node selection heuristics. sending snippet:
```
2026-02-11T11:05:12Z autoscaler controller ERROR selectNode: runtime: GC pause 120ms; cache-alloc growth
2026-02-11T11:06:03Z autoscaler controller WARN leader-election: failed to renew lease: context deadline exceeded
```
matt-infra: provider replied with intermittent 429s and 500s for create_instances. Also saw a parallel AZ (eu-west-2a) with transient capacity shortages for G4-type instances.
liam-sre: mitigation plan (short term):
- step1: enable emergency-burst pool (pre-warmed small T4s) and route low-latency critical traffic there. (matt)
- step2: reduce low-priority backend concurrency by 50% to free up queue slots. (sara)
- step3: manually scale GPU pool by +6 nodes in eu-west-2b/c where capacity is available. (matt)
- step4: restart autoscaler controller once logs harvested to avoid immediate re-crash. (jenna)
jenna-runtime: I’ll pull a heap profile and bump controller JVM flags (reduce metaspace growth) before restart. Doing it now.
matt-infra: manual scale-up initiated: launched 4 nodes in eu-west-2b, 3 nodes in eu-west-2c. provider returned 2 transient 429s but final state is 7/7 healthy.
sara-oncall: applied throttles on /v1/generate-batch for free-tier and background routes. rate limits now enforced.
liam-sre: routing change: traffic-split 90%->main pool, 10%->emergency-burst. Observed queue drop from 18k to 6.1k over 7m. latency p95 dropped from 9.5s to 4.2s.
carol-cs: Updated customers: told them we enabled temporary throttling and are adding capacity; asked for any immediate impact reports. They appreciated the update.
opsbot: Metric snapshot: queued_requests=6.1k, avg_latency=4.8s, error_rate=0.7% (post-mitigation).
liam-sre: root cause hypothesis: interplay of provider-side instance capacity pressure (one AZ degraded) + autoscaler controller memory growth bug that causes leader lease loss under load, preventing timely scale-up. Secondary factor: lack of emergency pre-warmed nodes for this growth pattern.
jenna-runtime: post-restart health: controller stable for 12m, no OOMs so far after JVM flag changes. I’ll keep heapprof running for 1h.
matt-infra: created short-term provider mitigation play: if >10% provision 429s in region, auto-switch to multi-AZ placement and backoff to avoid retries. filing PR for infra-ops.
sara-oncall: current customer impact: partial (degraded) for some long-running generation requests, P0 alerts for affected enterprise customers resolved to reduced severity after capacity added. marking as under control.
liam-sre: immediate action items (owners):
- A1: add pre-warmed emergency pool + runbook for fast routing (matt)
- A2: fix autoscaler GC/heap bloat + add memory alert (jenna)
- A3: add provider 429 circuit breaker and multi-AZ fallback (matt)
- A4: add a dashboard for leader-lease renewals and controller restarts (liam)
- A5: update customer-facing incident note and CS playbook (carol)
(ETA for initial patches: 72h)
carol-cs: drafting customer post-incident message now, will share for review.
liam-sre: follow-up postmortem notes to include timeline, root cause, mitigation, and action items. Schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:30 UTC. Invite: eng-sre, eng-runtime, infra, product support.
evan-eng: looping in product to evaluate feature-level rate-limits and graceful degradation options (simpler model fallback for heavy tails).
liam-sre: closing live thread — moving to incident channel for longer-running investigation. keep updates in the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
